title: Regional queueback analysis - Aug 2026
content:
Summary:
This sheet collects the raw pulls and quick analysis for the Aug 12–13 regional capacity incident that manifested as persistent queue growth ("queueback") in eu-west and us-central. Unlike prior incidents that were transient bursts, this event showed a long tail of queued requests on a narrow subset of pods. Purpose is to capture metric extracts, sampling windows, naive root-cause signals, and quick mitigation playbook so the oncall + infra team can iterate.

Top-level findings (quick):
- Primary observable: steady increase in "queued_requests" starting 2026-08-12 03:40 UTC, peaking 90–120s queue depth on eu-west pool nodes by 2026-08-12 06:12 UTC.
- Affected models: rwd-7b-int8 (quantized variant) and rwd-13b-fp16 in mixed pools due to autoscaler mixing policy change from July rollout.
- Immediate cause hypothesis: kernel selection regression + batching policy mismatch that increased per-request GPU setup time (kernel warm-up) and reduced effective throughput, which caused continuous backlog.
- Secondary contributor: regional routing fallback that pushed more traffic into eu-west when us-west had transient throttles (see linked throttle trace).

Data pulls included below (sources and queries):
1) Aggregated queue depth by pod (minute resolution)
- Query (PromQL simplified):
  sum_over_time(gateway_requests_queued{region=~"eu-west|us-central"}[1m]) by (pod, region)
- Sample CSV rows:
  timestamp,region,pod,queued_count
  2026-08-12T05:58:00Z,eu-west,pod-gpu-a-17,83
  2026-08-12T06:00:00Z,eu-west,pod-gpu-a-17,98
  2026-08-12T06:02:00Z,eu-west,pod-gpu-a-17,112

2) GPU utilization vs kernel latency (10s buckets)
- Query: custom_exporter.kernel_latency_ms{kernel="matmul"} and node_gpu_utilization_percent
- Notable: kernel latency 1.8–2.6x baseline on affected pods during ramp window.

3) Autoscaler decision logs (k8s events + autoscaler)
- Pull: kubectl get events --namespace=redwood-serving --since=48h -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.reason=="ScaleUp" or .reason=="ScaleDown")'
- Observed: scaler increased replica count in eu-west by +6 between 04:30–05:10 UTC but most new pods reported "init: kernel-cache-miss" for the first 2–3 minutes which reduced their immediate capacity contribution.

4) Router traces / route fallbacks
- Extracted from router logs: fallback_count{region="us-west", target_region="eu-west"} spike aligning with 03:38–04:10 UTC window.

Sampling windows and datasets attached (as raw pulls):
- window-A: 2026-08-12T03:00:00Z -> 2026-08-12T07:00:00Z (high-fidelity, 10s samples)
- window-B: 2026-08-11T00:00:00Z -> 2026-08-13T00:00:00Z (24h overview, 60s samples)

Quick correlation checklist (how we correlated metrics):
- Step 1: Confirm queueback via gateway queued metric + histogram of request wait times.
- Step 2: Cross-check pod start times (kube events) to see if cold start wave overlaps.
- Step 3: Kernel latency histograms per pod to detect unusual warm-up or JIT-like effects post-upgrade.
- Step 4: Router fallback traces to determine cross-region traffic shifts.
- Step 5: Model variant mix on pods (via labeling) to see if quantized models concentrated on particular nodes.

Preliminary root cause narrative (work-in-progress):
- On 2026-08-11 we rolled a minor autoscaler policy change (PR #1338) which relaxed bin-packing heuristics and allowed mixed-model scheduling in the same ASG.
- That change increased the probability that int8-quantized and fp16 models land on same pods. For a subset of kernels, the runtime selects different CUDA kernels depending on active model variant; when a pod served its first int8 inference after being idle it triggered a kernel path with higher warm-up latency (kernel cache cold miss).
- Combined with increased routed traffic from region fallback, the net effect was pods returning to service slower than autoscaler assumed, creating an accumulating queue.

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-08-12 06:05 UTC: Apply temporary routing cap on eu-west (route split 80/20 to us-west where capacity healthy) — reduced inbound rate to eu-west by ~22% within 10m.
- 2026-08-12 06:18 UTC: Roll back autoscaler policy (revert PR #1338) to restore previous placement heuristics.
- 2026-08-12 06:36 UTC: Hotpatch on affected pool to pre-warm common kernels on new pods (init hook that runs small matmul workload).
- Post-mitigation: queue depth returned to baseline by ~2026-08-12 07:40 UTC.

Proposed long-term actions (engineering backlog items):
- A: Add kernel warm-up probe to new-pod lifecycle; instrument kernel cache miss counters and expose as SLO guard (ticket INFRA-2485).
- B: Add autoscaler safety: treat pods in first 5 minutes as partial-capacity (factor in bootstrap latency).
- C: Improve router fallback heuristics so fallback only increases route weight gradually when target region shows stable capacity.
- D: Add a canary placement policy for mixed-model scheduling and run stress tests before global rollout.

Data quality and caveats:
- Some kernel_latency metrics were sampled at 15s intervals in older exporter version; we stitched using linear interpolation — treat high-frequency numbers as indicative, not exact.
- Pod labeling for model-variant is best-effort (inferred from recent pulls) and may miss rapid reassignments.

Appendix: useful commands and panels
- Pull per-pod queued metric CSV (example):
  for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=redwood-serving -o name); do echo $p; curl -s "http://prom-api/api/v1/query_range?query=sum(gateway_requests_queued{pod=\"$p\"})&start=...&end=...&step=10"; done
- Kernel warm-up panels: Grafana dashboard "gpu-kernel-warmup" uid: abc123
- Relevant PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1338 (autoscaler change), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/674 (kernel scheduling tweak)

Open questions for postmortem:
- Q1: Why did kernel cache miss rate spike for a subset of pods and not others with identical images? (potential hypothesis: micro-variations in host CUDA driver state).
- Q2: Were there concurrent infra maintenance operations (driver/kmod updates) in eu-west that coincided? Need ops audit.
- Q3: Exact contribution of router fallback vs local throughput drop — produce a counterfactual where fallback was disabled and simulate queue trajectory.

Next steps (owners):
- Maya: collate full CSV pulls and upload to artifact store (by 2026-08-16).
- Ethan: open INFRA-2485 for kernel warm-up probe spec (by 2026-08-18).
- Sofia: run placement canary job on staging with mixed-model scheduling (by 2026-08-20).

Notes to self: this is rough; we'll refine after correlating with node-level dmesg and driver logs. Save raw exports under /artifacts/infra/incidents/2026-08-12-queueback/"
